# A5 — Integration Evidence

| | |
|---|---|
| **Team** | Pod 5 — Alumni Network (Team 19), Mae Fah Luang University |
| **Members** | Phyo Sithu · Phyo Wai Yan Lin Zaw · Nyan Linn Htet · Khun Be Be R Zar Ni · Aye Min Aung |
| **Partner** | Team 17 — Internship Management |
| **Our base URL** | `https://alumni-network-integration.phyo2lay.workers.dev` |
| **Partner base URL** | `https://team17-internship.vercel.app` |
| **Date** | 2026-09-21 |

All evidence is captured directly from production (live deployment + production D1), except
Section 6 (Degradation), which was run locally against `wrangler dev` to safely point at a
deliberately-broken URL without touching the live service. Most "response body" evidence below
is a raw HTTP transcript — every value is copy-pasted from an actual `curl` / `wrangler d1` run,
not reconstructed by hand. Sections 1, 2 and 3 also include real screenshots (embedded inline as
base64, so this file is self-contained): a direct browser hit on Section 1's endpoint, and Team
17's own Postman session for Sections 2–3, corroborating our data from their side of the wire.

## Summary

| # | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Consumer Proof — we call Team 17 | ✅ Pass |
| 2 | Provider Proof — Team 17 calls us | ✅ Pass |
| 3 | Webhook Receiver — signed event in, verified + stored | ✅ Pass |
| 4 | Webhook Sender — signed event out, accepted | ✅ Pass |
| 5 | Idempotency — retried request, single row created | ✅ Pass |
| 6 | Degradation — broken dependency handled, auto-recovered | ✅ Pass |

## 2. Provider Proof

*Team 17 calls our endpoint.*

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Our endpoint | `GET https://alumni-network-integration.phyo2lay.workers.dev/api/integration/status` |
| Internal self-test timestamp | `2026-09-21T14:53:41Z` |
| Response status | `200 OK` |
| Partner confirmation | Team 17 confirmed calling this endpoint successfully (2026-09-21) |

**Internal request log (self-test, same route Team 17 hits):**

```json
{ "team": "pod5-alumni-network", "service": "alumni-network-integration", "version": "0.1", "status": "ok" }
```

Independently verified beyond their word: a real payload from their system reached our
infrastructure (Section 3) — stronger proof than a status-check claim alone.

**Partner-side screenshot** — Team 17's own Postman call to their `status-events` trigger
endpoint, showing the `webhook_delivery` object they logged for the call they made to us:

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," width="700" alt="Team 17's Postman screenshot showing webhook delivery to our receiver">

Key fields from their response: `webhook_delivery.state: "delivered"`, `status: 200`,
`response: "{\"received\":true}"` — that response string is exactly what our receiver returns,
confirmed independently from their side of the wire.

## 3. Webhook Receiver

*Team 17 sends us a webhook; we verify and store it.*

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Endpoint | `POST /api/webhooks/partner` |
| Secret verification | HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body, keyed with our `WEBHOOK_SECRET`, timing-safe compared against `X-Webhook-Signature` |
| Bad signature test | `401 {"error":"invalid signature"}` (confirmed during development) |
| Received timestamp | `2026-09-21T10:40:39.331Z` |
| Verification result | Signature valid → stored |

**Incoming payload** (real, from Team 17's system — not a value we generated):

```json
{
  "id": "f5d04873-f9e9-4fbf-bf87-f3e1d92ab702",
  "type": "internship.status_changed",
  "data": {
    "demo": true,
    "application_id": "app_demo_001",
    "current_status": "approved",
    "previous_status": "under_review"
  }
}
```

**Stored log** (queried directly from production D1, not just the HTTP response):

```sql
-- $ npx wrangler d1 execute alumni-network-db --remote --command
--   "SELECT source_id, event_type, payload, received_at FROM webhook_events ORDER BY received_at DESC"

source_id:    f5d04873-f9e9-4fbf-bf87-f3e1d92ab702
event_type:   internship.status_changed
received_at:  2026-09-21T10:40:39.331Z
```

**Corroborating screenshot from the sender's side** (Team 17's Postman, same event):

*(Same screenshot as embedded in [Section 2](#2-provider-proof) above — shown there to avoid duplicating a ~1MB image twice in one file.)*

Their `event_id` (`f5d04873-f9e9-...`) and `occurred_at` (`10:40:39.124Z`) match our stored
row exactly; their `attempted_at` (`10:40:39.673Z`) is a few hundred ms after our `received_at`
(`10:40:39.331Z`) — consistent with real network round-trip timing, not a fabricated match.

## 4. Webhook Sender

*We send Team 17 a webhook.*

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Trigger | `POST /api/webhooks/send-test` (manual trigger for this lab) |
| Partner webhook URL | `https://team17-internship.vercel.app/api/webhooks/partner` |
| Header used | `X-Webhook-Secret: <their shared secret>` — their receiver's required format, distinct from the HMAC signature ours expects (Section 3) |
| Sent timestamp | `2026-09-21T14:53:49Z` |
| Partner response status | `200 OK` |

**Outgoing payload:**

```json
{
  "event_id": "alumni-team17-handshake-1790002429737",
  "event_type": "partner.updated",
  "occurred_at": "2026-09-21T14:53:49Z",
  "source": "pod5-alumni-network",
  "data": { "resource_id": "alumni-demo-001", "status": "updated" }
}
```

**Partner response:**

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "message": "Webhook accepted",
  "event_id": "alumni-team17-handshake-1790002429737",
  "duplicate": false
}
```

## 5. Idempotency Proof

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Endpoint | `POST /api/connections` |
| Idempotency key | `a5-evidence-1790002432` |
| Request 1 status | `201 Created` |
| Request 2 status | `200 OK` (same key + body, sent 1s later) |
| DB row count for this key | `1` |

**Request 1 response:**

```json
{ "id": "bb1a82d4-1f98-4e16-be13-305142a4afb4", "studentId": 1, "alumniId": 1, "createdAt": "2026-09-21T14:53:52.850Z" }
```

**Request 2 response** (identical `id` and `createdAt` — no re-run of the create logic):

```json
{ "id": "bb1a82d4-1f98-4e16-be13-305142a4afb4", "studentId": 1, "alumniId": 1, "createdAt": "2026-09-21T14:53:52.850Z" }
```

**DB proof of single creation:**

```sql
-- $ npx wrangler d1 execute alumni-network-db --remote --command
--   "SELECT COUNT(*) as row_count FROM idempotency_keys WHERE key = 'a5-evidence-1790002432'"

row_count: 1
```

Two requests, one stored row — the `Idempotency-Key` header, not luck, prevented the duplicate.

## 6. Degradation Proof

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Broken dependency | `PARTNER_API_URL` pointed at an unroutable address, simulating Team 17 down |
| Exercised via | `GET /api/partner/status` |
| Breakage window | `2026-09-21T14:54:16Z` → `14:54:21Z` (5.03s, matches `AbortSignal.timeout(5000)`) |
| Fallback status | `504 Gateway Timeout` |
| Recovery timestamp | `2026-09-21T14:54:31Z` |
| Recovery method | dependency URL restored — no code change, redeploy, or restart |
| Unrelated routes during outage | `/api/integration/status` stayed `200` throughout |

**Fallback JSON output:**

```json
{ "error": "partner unreachable", "detail": "TimeoutError: The operation was aborted due to timeout" }
```

**Automatic recovery — next call to the same route, immediately after:**

```json
{ "success": true, "data": { "team": "team17-internship-management", "status": "ok" } }
```
